hero.intro: I configure servers, plugins, bots and permissions. Then I sort out the staff side of things, so the whole lot keeps running once I'm gone. Been doing this since 2019.

panel.title: Taking on new builds
panel.body: I've got room for two bigger jobs this month, either a full network setup or a Discord rebuild. Smaller things like a permissions fix usually take a few days.
panel.footnote: Every job ends with written docs and a call to walk your team through it. The whole point is that you don't need me afterwards.

pillars.title: What I actually do.
pillars.kicker: Most servers I get called into aren't broken because of bad plugins. They're broken because nobody ever wrote down how any of it works.

items.title: Server configuration
items.body: Paper and Purpur tuning, Velocity proxies, world management, and the performance work that keeps tick times flat once the server actually fills up.

items.title: Plugin configuration
items.body: Permissions, economies, custom items, quests, menus. Most of the job is getting twenty plugins to stop fighting over the same events.

items.title: Discord engineering
items.body: Channel structure, role hierarchies, onboarding, tickets, and enough automation that moderating stops being a second job for someone.

items.title: Staff and team management
items.body: Hiring rubrics, training, shift rotas, escalation ladders. Teams that can make a call at 3am without waiting for an owner to wake up.

items.title: Community operations
items.body: Rules that hold up when somebody argues with them, appeals that stay fair, and events that bring people back without paying them to log in.

items.title: Hosting and infrastructure
items.body: Panels, backups, staged migrations, monitoring. It's the boring layer, and it decides how bad a bad night ends up being.

timelinePreview.title: Where I've worked.
timelinePreview.kicker: The networks and communities I've set up, run, or been called in to rescue.

workPreview.title: On the bench right now.
workPreview.kicker: Three jobs in progress, with an honest read on how far along each one really is.

skillsPreview.title: What I'm good at.
skillsPreview.kicker: The technical side keeps a server up. The management side is what keeps people logging back into it.

reviewsPreview.title: What clients said.
reviewsPreview.kicker: Feedback from owners, community managers and staff leads I've worked with.

closing.title: Got something that needs sorting?
closing.body: Tell me what you're running and what's going wrong with it. If I'm not the right person for the job, I'll say so.
